## Summary

Jogaila (c. 1362 - 1 June 1434), baptised Władysław, is the nephew who kills Kęstutis, the cousin who spends fifty years half-fearing Vytautas, and the king who founds a dynasty. When the reader first meets him in Book I he is a young, anxious Grand Duke living in his father's shadow, convinced that Lithuania must become Christian and Western to survive and that betrayal is a higher form of loyalty to the future. He is the Shadow-Seller's first and longest-lasting customer. In the saga he is the mortal antagonist of Book I (with [Skirgaila](skirgaila.qmd) as his hands) and the man whose baptism ends the Silent Pact.

## Appearance & tells

Slender and frail-looking but restless, with dark intelligent eyes that never settle. He wears fine velvets and silks in the Western style against his cousins' furs and leather, and is clean-shaven where the pagan dukes keep beards. Tells: he cannot look at Kęstutis's silver wolf (Book I ch. 26; Book III ch. 20, where it costs him "everything he has" to hold Vytautas's eyes); a crushing pressure on his chest in sacred groves; crows that follow him; a court *burtininkas* who has never cast him a bad lot. By the end, an old man with spectacles in his hand, looking at the floor in front of his feet at Vytautas's funeral (Book V ch. 2).

## Want · Need · Lie · Truth

| | |
|---|---|
| **Want** (external) | The Lithuanian throne and a Western dynasty: to unite Lithuania and Poland into a power rivalling the Holy Roman Empire, and to keep the Order from finishing Lithuania. |
| **Need** (internal) | To trust the one man he cannot buy: to stop seeing Krėva everywhere. |
| **Lie** they believe | That baptism and the Polish crown are a cheap price: that betrayal is only a higher loyalty to the future. |
| **Truth** they learn (or refuse) | What a bargain with the Shadow-Seller really buys: a line that inherits the crown and loses the land. He half-learns it in his old age, outliving Vytautas still guilty (Book IV; Book V ch. 12). |

## Arc by book

- **Book I (1377-87), antagonist:** inherits the throne (1377); signs the secret Treaty of Dovydiškės with the Order (31 May 1380); is caught and freed by Kęstutis in autumn 1381 (the "mercy" that will pay off at Krėva); retakes Vilnius on 12 June 1382; seizes Kęstutis and Vytautas at his camp near Trakai (early August 1382); is haunted by Krėva (ch. 26); signs the Union of Krėva (14 Aug 1385) and is baptised, married and crowned in Kraków (1386); puts out the Šventaragis flame (1387).
- **Book II:** the distant king; makes Ostrów (4 Aug 1392) with Vytautas (ch. 10); Jadwiga dies (ch. 21).
- **Book III:** the reconciliation: Vilnius-Radom (1401, ch. 3), the Brest council (ch. 13), and at Grunwald beside Vytautas (ch. 18-24).
- **Book IV:** at Lutsk (1429) he is the one who offers and then withdraws the crown (ch. 18, 19, 24, 26); outlives Vytautas.
- **Book V:** dies at Gródek, 1 June 1434, after hearing a nightingale (ch. 12).
- **Book VI:** seen as a boy, taught by Uliana at six to hide what he wants (ch. 15), and as Algirdas's chosen heir at fifteen (ch. 27, 28).

## Power & magic

Tier 0 (*Paprastas*): no gift. His power is **bought**: the 1380 bargain with the [Shadow-Seller](../forces/shadow_seller.qmd) is "the easy way" of the trap, and its price is that his line inherits the crown and loses the land ([Sandėris](../magic/bargain.qmd)). He holds the [golden chain](../artifacts/golden_chain.qmd) sent as a "gift" with the 1382 envoys. Henė's stone for him is the last he holds in Book V. His ambition feeds the [Gold-Glutton](../forces/gold_glutton.qmd) and draws the [White Silence](../forces/white_silence.qmd). Visible costs: four wives and sons only from the last; the grove pressure; the crows. The [Root-Mother](../forces/root_mother.qmd) regards him as a tumour in her side.

## Record vs saga

- **[Record]:** Born c. 1362 (Tęgowski 1999, the post-1990 consensus; the older view is c. 1352), Grand Duke of Lithuania from 1377 (co-ruling with Kęstutis), baptised Władysław in Kraków on 15 Feb 1386, married Jadwiga on 18 Feb and crowned King of Poland on 4 Mar 1386; ruler of Lithuania until 1392, then overlord of Vytautas. He signed the Treaty of Dovydiškės with the Order on 31 May 1380, regained Vilnius on 12 June 1382, when Hanul and the townspeople handed him the city while Kęstutis was away fighting Kaributas, and had Kęstutis and Vytautas seized on 3 Aug 1382 at his camp near Trakai; Kęstutis was found dead at Krėva on 15 Aug (the official story: suicide). Union of Krėva (14 Aug 1385); baptism of Lithuania (1387); Ostrów (1392); Grunwald (15 Jul 1410); Horodło (1413); Lutsk (1429). Wives: Jadwiga (d. 1399), Anna of Celje (d. 1416), Elżbieta Granowska (d. 1420), Sophia of Halshany (m. 1422), mother of Władysław III and Casimir IV. Died 1 Jun 1434 at Gródek (Horodok) near Lviv. See [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jogaila).
- **[Saga invention]:** The Shadow-Seller's bargain and the golden chain used on Kęstutis; the strangulation (the record gives murder by strangulation as one side of a disagreement, suicide as the official story); the crows and the grove pressure; his inability to look at the silver wolf; the court burtininkas. The nightingale at Gródek is a historical anecdote (Długosz). The saga chooses 1362 for his birth; it never states his age except in Book I ch. 5 (four, in 1366).

## Pronunciation

**jo-GAI-la** (/joˈɡɐɪɫɐ/), English respelling *yo-GUY-lah*; stress on the second syllable. The dynasty *Jogailaičiai*: jo-gai-LAI-čiai, *yo-guy-LYE-chay*. Polish *Jagiełło*, baptismal *Władysław*. [world_rules/pronunciation_lexicon.json]

## Appearances

**Book I:** ch. 1-7, 9-13, 17, 26 (the silver wolf), 28, 28b (Union of Krėva), 29, 30 and the prologue. **Book II:** ch. 1, 2, 4, 10 (Ostrów), 21, 22, 29 and the afterword. **Book III:** ch. 3 (Vilnius and Radom), 6, 8, 13, 18, 20, 24 (a long chapter from his side), 25, 27, 30 and the afterword. **Book IV:** ch. 3, 13, 14, 18, 19 (Lutsk), 24, 26 (Last Meeting). **Book V:** ch. 2, 3, 6, 12 (the nightingale), 18, 24 and the afterword. **Book VI:** ch. 15, 25-30 (as a boy and Algirdas's heir). Continuity: Henė's stone for him is his only remaining one in Book V (ch. 8).
